newsitem.title: INDIA: India to consider $335 mln airport project soon.
newsitem.headline: India to consider $335 mln airport project soon.

text.p: Indian Civil Aviation Minister C.M. Ibrahim has said his ministry will soon consider a proposed 12 billion rupee ($335 million) international airport in the capital of southern Karnataka state, Bangalore.
Ibrahim told Reuters his ministry will hold a meeting on the proposal no later than February 20.

The proposed project involving Raytheon Co of the United States, Singapore Airport Authority and India's Tata group is caught in a dispute between the federal and Karnataka governments, officials said.
"If the consortium is not agreeable to our terms by February 20, they will lose the project," Ibrahim said after meeting Karnataka Industry Minister R.V. Deshpande in Bangalore late on Tuesday.
The Civil Aviation Ministry has opposed the agreement between the Karnataka government and the Tata-led consortium which would allow the consortium to operate on a build-own-operate (BOO) basis.
Ibrahim has insisted that it must be on a build-operate-own-transfer (BOOT) basis, officials said.
"I cannot jeopardise the interests of the country. I would go according to the rules," Ibrahim said.
"It is an international practice. Nowhere a private company is allowed to operate on a BOO basis," Ibrahim added.
Deshpande said Ibrahim's statements were sending confusing signals to foreign investors and a painting a bad image of the state government.
"Definitely, it is sending wrong signals to foreign investors. It is giving us a bad image," Deshpande said. ($1 = 35.8 rupees)
